system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Two-round self-training with counterfactual occlusion masks from the jointly trained model
SUMMARY: Train MVFA on initial pseudo-masks, then regenerate the masks by counterfactual occlusion attribution of the jointly trained model's detection branch and retrain once.
HYPOTHESIS: Second-round occlusion masks from the jointly trained model have at least 8 points higher Dice against true masks than first-round nearest-neighbour masks and at least 4 points higher than occlusion masks from a detection-only model, and the round-2 MVFA recovers at least 92% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC.
RATIONALE: The occlusion parent derives masks from a detection branch trained alone; the self-training parent regenerates masks from adapted features after a first round. After a first joint round, the detection branch has been trained alongside segmentation targets, so its patch evidence should be sharper, and occlusion attribution of that branch is a causal signal that does not reuse the segmentation branch's own predictions (avoiding the confirmation bias of plain self-training). The combination therefore improves both parents: better attributions than a detection-only model and less self-confirmation than feature-based regeneration.
METHOD: 1) Round 1: label-restricted pseudo-masks; train MVFA (both branches) as usual. 2) Occlusion: for each abnormal source image, for each patch p, replace the cached level features at p by their nearest normal-bank features and recompute the det branch's mean-pooled score; a_p = drop in score. 3) Masks: a_p above the 99th percentile of attributions on normal source-validation images; abnormal images only. 4) Round 2: retrain from the CLIP initialisation on the new masks. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; round 1; round 2 with feature-based regeneration; round 2 with occlusion masks from the joint model; occlusion masks from a det-only model. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice per round, trained pixel AUROC, Dice. Falsified if joint-model occlusion masks do not beat both alternatives by the stated margins.

Idea B:
TITLE: Counterfactual normal-twin differencing: pseudo-masks from each abnormal image's most similar normal image
SUMMARY: For every abnormal source image, retrieve the most similar normal image of the same dataset, align it, and mark as anomalous the patches whose CLIP features differ most from the aligned twin, giving pseudo-masks that compare like with like.
HYPOTHESIS: Twin-differencing pseudo-masks reach at least 8 points higher Dice against true masks than bank-wide nearest-neighbour pseudo-masks on BrainMRI and LiverCT, where slices are anatomically comparable, and MVFA trained on them recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: Both parents ask a counterfactual question, what would this image look like if it were normal, through the detection branch. A more direct answer is available in BMAD: many normal images of the same anatomy exist, and the most similar one, aligned to the abnormal image, is an empirical counterfactual (similar to registration-based few-shot anomaly detection). Comparing each patch with the corresponding patch of the aligned twin, rather than with any patch of the bank, removes false positives from anatomy that is normal but rare at that position, which bank-wide nearest-neighbour distances cannot distinguish.
METHOD: 1) Global descriptor: mean of frozen CLIP level-4 patch features. 2) For each abnormal source image, retrieve the 3 most similar normal training images of the same dataset (cosine). 3) Align each twin by an affine transform estimated with OpenCV ECC on downsampled intensity images (identity if ECC fails). 4) Patch difference: d_p = min over twins and over a 3x3 patch neighbourhood of 1 - cos(f_p, f_twin,q). 5) Threshold at the 99th percentile of the same statistic on normal source-validation images paired with their own twins; abnormal images only. 6) train_zero.py unchanged. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; bank-wide NN pseudo-masks; twin differencing with 1 and 3 twins; with and without alignment. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice per dataset, trained pixel AUROC, Dice. Falsified if twin differencing does not beat bank-wide NN by 8 Dice points on BrainMRI or LiverCT.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
